cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for bars, markets and small trattorie. A coperto (cover charge) is normal; tipping is optional.
name: Matera
tagline: Ancient cave city carved into a ravine
summary: Matera is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth, its Sassi cave dwellings stacked up the side of a ravine. Explore rock-cut churches with Byzantine frescoes, step inside a furnished cave house, sleep in a cave hotel, and cross the gorge to the Murgia park for the view back at the lit-up town.
seasonNote: Spring and early autumn are ideal; summer is hot, and the 2 July Bruna festival fills the town.
arrival: Bari airport is about 1 hour by shuttle bus or car; Ferrovie Appulo Lucane trains run from Bari.
gettingAround: Walk the Sassi (lots of steps); taxis or a car for the Murgia park.
foodTip: Pane di Matera bread, crapiata bean soup, peperoni cruschi (crispy dried peppers) and orecchiette.
baseArea: Sasso Barisano or Sasso Caveoso, in a cave hotel

connections.note: About an hour to Alberobello and the Bari area.

items.name: Sassi di Matera
items.summary: Two cave districts of houses, churches and stairways cut into the rock.
items.tip: Walk them at dawn and again after dark when they are lit.

items.name: Belvedere Luigi Guerricchio
items.summary: Viewpoint over the Sassi and the cathedral bell tower.
items.tip: Come at blue hour.

items.name: Casa Grotta di Vico Solitario
items.summary: Furnished cave house showing how families and animals lived together until the 1950s.
items.tip: Read the story of the 1950s evacuation.

items.name: Santa Maria de Idris
items.summary: Rock church on a crag with faded frescoes in the tunnel to San Giovanni in Monterrone.
items.expect: Combined tickets with other rock churches.
items.tip: Buy the rock churches pass.

items.name: Palombaro Lungo
items.summary: Huge underground cistern beneath the main square.
items.tip: Short tour; queue early.

items.name: Murgia Materana Park
items.summary: Wild plateau across the ravine with cave churches and the best view of Matera.
items.expect: Steep path down and up from the Sassi.
items.tip: Drive to Belvedere di Murgia Timone for sunset.

items.name: Matera Cathedral
items.summary: 13th-century Apulian Romanesque cathedral on the ridge between the two Sassi.
items.tip: Look at the rose window outside.

items.name: Pane di Matera and crapiata
items.summary: Matera's crusty durum-wheat bread and a soup of many beans and grains.
items.tip: Ask for peperoni cruschi too.

items.name: Orecchiette and cavatelli
items.summary: Hand-made pasta with turnip greens or ragù.
items.tip: Cave restaurants make a memorable dinner.

items.name: Aperitivo with a view
items.summary: Terrace bars above the Sassi for a spritz at sunset.
items.tip: Arrive early for a front table.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for bars, markets and small trattorie. A coperto (cover charge) is normal; tipping is optional.
name: Lecce
tagline: Baroque in honey-coloured stone, and the beaches of Salento
summary: Lecce is the Florence of the South, a city of extravagant Baroque churches carved from soft golden stone. See the façade of Santa Croce and the Piazza del Duomo, peer into a half-buried Roman amphitheatre, eat pasticciotto for breakfast, and spend afternoons at Salento's coves at Otranto, Torre Sant'Andrea and Gallipoli.
seasonNote: June and September for beaches; August is crowded and hot.
arrival: Trains from Bari take 1h30; Brindisi airport is 40 minutes away.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; a car or regional trains and buses for the Salento coast.
foodTip: Pasticciotto custard pastry, rustico leccese, ciceri e tria (chickpea pasta) and caffè leccese with almond milk.
buyTip: Papier-mâché figures (cartapesta) and Salento wines like Primitivo and Negroamaro.

connections.note: Trains to Bari and the Valle d'Itria via Brindisi.

items.name: Basilica di Santa Croce
items.summary: Lecce's Baroque masterpiece, its façade crowded with carved animals and figures.
items.expect: Paid combined ticket for the churches.
items.tip: Look for the creatures on the balcony.

items.name: Piazza del Duomo
items.summary: Enclosed square with the cathedral, bell tower and bishop's palace.
items.tip: Visit after dark when it glows.

items.name: Roman Amphitheatre and Piazza Sant'Oronzo
items.summary: Half-excavated Roman amphitheatre sunk into the main square.
items.tip: Coffee in the square after.

items.name: Museo Faggiano
items.summary: A house where a man fixing a pipe found 2,000 years of layers beneath the floor.
items.tip: Climb the tower for the rooftops.

items.name: Otranto
items.summary: Walled seaside town with a cathedral floor mosaic of the Tree of Life.
items.tip: See the chapel of the martyrs, then swim.

items.name: Grotta della Poesia
items.summary: Natural sea pool in the limestone where people jump into clear water.
items.tip: Go early morning.

items.name: Gallipoli
items.summary: Island old town on the Ionian Sea with sunsets and seafood.
items.tip: Eat raw sea urchins at the fish market.

items.name: Pasticciotto
items.summary: Warm shortcrust pastry filled with custard, Lecce's breakfast.
items.tip: Pair with caffè leccese (iced coffee with almond milk).

items.name: Rustico leccese
items.summary: Puff pastry stuffed with béchamel, mozzarella and tomato.
items.tip: Eat it hot.

items.name: Ciceri e tria
items.summary: Chickpeas with fresh and fried pasta, a Salento classic.
items.tip: Pair with Negroamaro.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for bars, markets and small trattorie. A coperto (cover charge) is normal; tipping is optional.
name: Taormina
tagline: Greek theatre above the sea with Etna behind
summary: Taormina is a Sicilian hill town on a terrace above the Ionian Sea, with Mount Etna smoking in the distance. Sit in the Greek theatre for one of the world's great views, stroll the Corso Umberto, take the cable car down to Isola Bella, and day-trip to Etna's craters and the Alcantara gorges.
seasonNote: Spring and early autumn; July and August are busy, and the theatre hosts summer concerts.
arrival: Catania airport is about 1 hour by bus; trains stop at Taormina-Giardini below the town.
gettingAround: Walk the town; cable car to the beach; buses or tours for Etna.
foodTip: Granita with brioche, arancini, cannoli and pasta alla Norma.
buyTip: Ceramic heads (teste di moro) and Etna wines.

connections.note: Frequent buses from the airport and city.

items.name: Ancient Theatre of Taormina
items.summary: Greek-Roman theatre framing the sea and Mount Etna.
items.tip: Go at opening or late afternoon.
items.why: One of the world's great views.

items.name: Corso Umberto
items.summary: Main street between two medieval gates, with churches, palaces and shops.
items.tip: Walk it in the evening passeggiata.

items.name: Isola Bella
items.summary: Tiny nature reserve island joined to the beach by a sandbar.
items.tip: Take the cable car down.

items.name: Villa Comunale
items.summary: Gardens with follies and sea views, created by an English lady.
items.tip: Shady escape midday.

items.name: Castelmola
items.summary: Village above Taormina with castle ruins and almond wine.
items.tip: Try vino alla mandorla at Bar Turrisi.

items.name: Mount Etna
items.summary: Europe's most active volcano, with craters and lava fields to explore.
items.expect: Tour or car; cold at the top.
items.tip: Take the cable car from Rifugio Sapienza and a guided crater walk.

items.name: Alcantara Gorges
items.summary: Basalt column gorge carved by a river, with icy water.
items.expect: Paid entry or free public access.
items.tip: Wear water shoes.

items.name: Granita and brioche
items.summary: Almond, lemon or mulberry ice with a warm brioche for breakfast.
items.tip: Bam Bar is a famous spot.

items.name: Arancini
items.summary: Fried rice balls with ragù or butter and ham.
items.tip: Try the pistachio one.

items.name: Pasta alla Norma
items.summary: Pasta with fried aubergine, tomato and salted ricotta.
items.tip: Pair with an Etna Rosso.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted, but carry cash for bars, markets and small trattorie. A coperto (cover charge) is normal; tipping is optional.
name: Lake Garda
tagline: Italy's largest lake of castles, lemons and mountains
summary: Lake Garda stretches from the olive groves of Sirmione in the south to the fjord-like mountains of Riva in the north. See the moated Scaliger Castle at Sirmione, ride the cable car up Monte Baldo, wander the lemon houses of Limone, take the ferries between pastel villages, and visit the extravagant Vittoriale at Gardone.
seasonNote: May to September; many ferries and hotels reduce service in winter.
arrival: Trains to Desenzano or Peschiera from Milan (1 hour) and Verona (20 minutes); Verona airport is 30 minutes away.
gettingAround: Ferries and hydrofoils link the towns; buses run along the shore.
foodTip: Lake fish (coregone, trout), olive oil from Garda, risotto with tench, and Bardolino and Lugana wines.
buyTip: Garda olive oil and limoncello from Limone.

items.name: Sirmione and Scaliger Castle
items.summary: Moated 13th-century castle at the entrance to Sirmione's peninsula old town.
items.tip: Walk to the Grottoes of Catullus at the tip.

items.name: Grottoes of Catullus
items.summary: Ruins of a huge Roman villa on the peninsula tip above the lake.
items.tip: Look down at the Jamaica beach rocks.

items.name: Monte Baldo cable car
items.summary: Rotating cable car from Malcesine to the ridge 1,760 m above the lake.
items.tip: Go first thing; paragliders launch at the top.

items.name: Malcesine
items.summary: Lakeside village under a Scaliger castle.
items.tip: Climb the castle tower.

items.name: Limone sul Garda
items.summary: Village of terraced lemon houses under cliffs.
items.tip: Visit the Limonaia del Castèl.

items.name: Il Vittoriale degli Italiani
items.summary: Poet D'Annunzio's eccentric estate with a warship in the garden.
items.tip: Book the house tour.

items.name: Riva del Garda
items.summary: Mountain-walled town at the north end, a base for windsurfing and hiking.
items.tip: Hike the Ponale road.

items.name: Lake fish
items.summary: Coregone, trout and sardines from the lake, grilled or in pasta.
items.tip: Order with a glass of Lugana.

items.name: Bardolino wine
items.summary: Light red wine from the eastern shore with tastings in town and the wine museum.
items.tip: Visit the Zeni wine museum.

items.name: Gelato in Sirmione
items.summary: Gelato shops line the old town.
items.tip: Try lemon or pistachio.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry cash for beach bars and village trattorie.
name: Sardinia
tagline: Caribbean-clear coves, nuraghe towers and Cagliari
summary: Sardinia is a big island of white beaches and turquoise water, with its own language and 7,000 Bronze Age stone towers called nuraghi. Base in Cagliari for its old Castello quarter and Poetto beach, then see the giant UNESCO nuraghe of Su Nuraxi, the La Pelosa beach near Stintino, the Costa Smeralda and the coves of the Gulf of Orosei.
seasonNote: June and September for warm sea without August crowds; La Pelosa needs a booked ticket in summer.
arrival: Airports at Cagliari, Olbia and Alghero; ferries from Genoa, Livorno, Civitavecchia and Naples.
gettingAround: Rent a car; distances are long and buses are slow.
foodTip: Porceddu (spit-roast suckling pig), culurgiones dumplings, fregola with clams, pane carasau and seadas with honey.
buyTip: Cork crafts, filigree jewellery, Cannonau wine and pecorino sardo.

connections.note: Flights to Cagliari and Olbia; overnight ferry from Civitavecchia.

items.name: Cagliari Castello
items.summary: Walled hilltop quarter with the cathedral and the Bastione di Saint Remy terrace.
items.tip: Sunset drink on the Bastione.

items.name: Poetto beach
items.summary: Long city beach under the Devil's Saddle headland, with flamingos in the lagoon behind.
items.tip: Look for flamingos in Molentargius park.

items.name: Su Nuraxi di Barumini
items.summary: UNESCO Bronze Age fortress and village of stone towers.
items.expect: Guided tours only; 1 hour from Cagliari.
items.tip: Hats in summer; there is no shade.

items.name: La Pelosa beach
items.summary: Shallow turquoise water with a watchtower on an islet.
items.expect: Limited numbers in summer; book a ticket and bring a mat (towels on sand are banned).
items.tip: Go early or late.

items.name: Gulf of Orosei
items.summary: Cliff coast of coves like Cala Luna and Cala Goloritzé, reached by boat or hiking.
items.expect: Boats from Cala Gonone; Goloritzé is hike-only.
items.tip: Hike to Cala Goloritzé early.

items.name: Costa Smeralda
items.summary: Granite coast of emerald water and the glossy harbour of Porto Cervo.
items.tip: Boat to the La Maddalena islands.

items.name: Alghero old town
items.summary: Catalan-speaking walled port with sea ramparts and Neptune's Grotto nearby.
items.tip: Sunset on the ramparts.

items.name: Porceddu
items.summary: Suckling pig slow-roasted over myrtle wood until the skin crackles.
items.expect: Often order in advance at agriturismi.
items.tip: Have it at an agriturismo dinner.

items.name: Culurgiones
items.summary: Hand-pinched dumplings of potato, pecorino and mint with tomato sauce.
items.tip: Watch for the wheat-ear pleat.

items.name: Seadas
items.summary: Fried pastry filled with pecorino, drizzled with bitter honey.
items.tip: Pair with mirto liqueur.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere. Tip about 10 to 12.5 percent in restaurants if service is not included; not in pubs.
name: Lake District
tagline: Fells, lakes and the England of Wordsworth
summary: The Lake District is England's most loved mountain landscape, a national park of lakes and green fells. Cruise Windermere and Ullswater, climb Catbells or Helvellyn, visit Wordsworth's Dove Cottage and Beatrix Potter's Hill Top, and end each day in a slate-built pub by a log fire.
seasonNote: Late spring to early autumn; it rains often, so pack waterproofs. School holidays are busy.
arrival: Trains to Windermere via Oxenholme (London about 3 hours); Penrith for the north lakes.
gettingAround: Buses link the main towns; a car helps for the valleys but parking is tight.
foodTip: Cumberland sausage, sticky toffee pudding (invented at Cartmel), Grasmere gingerbread and Kendal Mint Cake.

items.name: Windermere lake cruise
items.summary: England's largest lake by steamer, from Bowness to Ambleside or Lakeside.
items.tip: Take the round trip and stop at Ambleside.

items.name: Catbells
items.summary: Short steep fell walk with views over Derwentwater.
items.tip: Take the launch from Keswick to Hawes End.

items.name: Derwentwater and Keswick
items.summary: Lake with wooded islands below a lively market town.
items.tip: Walk to Friar's Crag at sunset.

items.name: Castlerigg Stone Circle
items.summary: Neolithic stone circle ringed by mountains.
items.tip: Go at sunrise or sunset.

items.name: Dove Cottage and Grasmere
items.summary: Wordsworth's home in a village of slate cottages.
items.tip: Buy Grasmere gingerbread next to the church.

items.name: Hill Top
items.summary: Beatrix Potter's farmhouse, unchanged since she lived there.
items.tip: Book ahead in summer.

items.name: Ullswater and Aira Force
items.summary: Waterfall in a wooded gorge, then a steamer on Ullswater.
items.tip: Walk part of the Ullswater Way.

items.name: Helvellyn via Striding Edge
items.summary: England's most famous ridge scramble to a 950 m summit.
items.expect: Serious and exposed; only in good weather.
items.tip: Start early from Glenridding.

items.name: Sticky toffee pudding
items.summary: Date sponge drowned in toffee sauce, made famous at Cartmel village shop.
items.tip: Buy one from Cartmel to take home.

items.name: Lakeland pub dinner
items.summary: Slate pubs serving Cumberland sausage, pies and local ale.
items.tip: The Drunken Duck and Old Dungeon Ghyll are classics.

items.name: Grasmere Gingerbread
items.summary: Tiny shop baking a spicy chewy gingerbread since 1854.
items.tip: Buy a pack for walks.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere. Tip about 10 to 12.5 percent in restaurants if service is not included; not in pubs.
name: Cotswolds
tagline: Honey-stone villages in rolling English countryside
summary: The Cotswolds are rolling hills of golden-stone villages, sheep fields and old wool churches. Walk between Lower and Upper Slaughter, photograph Arlington Row in Bibury, browse Burford and Chipping Campden, tour Blenheim Palace and Sudeley Castle, and eat in thatched pubs.
seasonNote: Late spring and early autumn are prettiest; lavender blooms at Snowshill in July.
arrival: Trains from London Paddington to Moreton-in-Marsh or Kemble take about 1h30.
gettingAround: A car is easiest; buses are infrequent; walking paths join many villages.
foodTip: Pub roasts, Double Gloucester cheese and afternoon tea.
buyTip: Antiques in Stow and Tetbury, and local cheese.

items.name: Bibury and Arlington Row
items.summary: Row of 14th-century weavers' cottages by a stream.
items.tip: Come early morning.

items.name: Bourton-on-the-Water
items.summary: "Venice of the Cotswolds" with low bridges over the River Windrush.
items.tip: Walk to the Slaughters from here.

items.name: Lower and Upper Slaughter
items.summary: Two tiny villages with a working mill, joined by a field path.
items.tip: Walk the path from Bourton.

items.name: Chipping Campden
items.summary: Wool town with a curved high street and a 17th-century market hall.
items.tip: Start of the Cotswold Way.

items.name: Blenheim Palace
items.summary: Baroque palace where Churchill was born, in Capability Brown parkland.
items.tip: Allow a whole day with the park.

items.name: Castle Combe
items.summary: Village of stone cottages, often called England's prettiest.
items.tip: View from the bridge.

items.name: Sudeley Castle
items.summary: Castle and gardens where Henry VIII's last queen is buried.
items.tip: See Katherine Parr's chapel.

items.name: Broadway Tower
items.summary: Folly tower on a hill with views across many counties.
items.tip: Walk up from Broadway village.

items.name: Cotswold pub roast
items.summary: Roast beef and Yorkshire pudding in old coaching inns.
items.tip: Try a pub with a fire.

items.name: Afternoon tea
items.summary: Scones, clotted cream, jam and sandwiches in a tearoom.
items.tip: Cream first or jam first, you choose.

items.name: Double Gloucester cheese
items.summary: The region's firm orange cheese, from farm shops.
items.tip: Daylesford Organic farm shop is famous.
